name: Button group
description: A set of related buttons or links shown together, such as a primary and a secondary call to action. It groups them visually and, when useful, with role="group", but adds no keyboard behavior of its own.
summary: Related buttons or links kept together
aria: Toolbar (only if roving tabindex is needed)
researchNote: A CTA pair is not a toolbar

elements.name: Primary action
elements.description: The main link or button, first in source order

elements.name: Group
elements.description: Wrapper that sets spacing and alignment; gets role="group" and a label only when the grouping is meaningful

variants.caption: Stacked — full width on a narrow screen

usageNotes: Calls to action usually go somewhere, so make them <a href> links styled as buttons. Use <button> only for actions on the current page.

Don't add role="toolbar". The ARIA Authoring Practices toolbar pattern expects a single tab stop with arrow-key movement, which a pair of calls to action doesn't need. Each item stays in the normal tab order.
Add role="group" with aria-label only when the grouping tells screen reader users something, such as a set of actions for one item in a list.
Keep the source order the same as the visual order so reading and focus order match (WCAG 1.3.2, 2.4.3). Don't reverse the buttons with CSS alone.
For choosing one of several options, use a Segmented control. For several buttons that each stay pressed, use Toggle buttons.
